source_text: Οἱ ἐν Βιέννῃ καὶ Λουγδούνῳ τῆς Γαλλίας παροικοῦντες δοῦλοι Χριστοῦ, τοῖς κατὰ τὴν Ἀσίαν καὶ Φρυγίαν τὴν αὐτὴν τῆς ἀπολυτρώσεως ἡμῖν πίστιν καὶ ἐλπίδα ἔχουσιν ἀδελφοῖς, εἰρήνη καὶ χάρις καὶ δόξα ἀπὸ θεοῦ πατρὸς καὶ Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν.
pass_a_gloss: The slaves of Christ sojourning in Vienne and Lugdunum of Gaul, to the brothers in Asia and Phrygia having the same faith and hope of the redemption as us: peace and grace and glory from God Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.
pass_b_english: The servants of Christ sojourning at Vienne and Lyons in Gaul, to the brothers throughout Asia and Phrygia who share with us the same faith and hope in redemption, wish peace and grace and glory from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.

choices.why: present participle stresses ongoing temporary residence rather than native citizenship, fitting Christians in Gaul writing to Asia
genitive is possessive and relational; keeps the self-designation of belonging to Christ in a letter greeting
